subject: Operationalizing tiered transfer controls — phased DTIA attestation & timeline
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novamed.es>, Contracts <contracts@novamed.es>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:22:00 +0100
Subject: Operationalizing tiered transfer controls — phased DTIA attestation & timeline

Hi Marta / Novamed contracts team,

Thanks again for taking time during yesterday's call. Per our discussion, Novamed has a handful of constrained data categories that will require either onshore processing or an explicit DTIA (contract-level attestation) for cross-border routing. To keep the procurement cadence moving, we propose a phased path:

1) Phase A (Week 1-2): onboarding checklist + evidence index — confirm scope and any processor carveouts.
2) Phase B (Week 2-4): DTIA template + Novamed attestation (targeted controls only).
3) Phase C (Week 4-6): production routing rules & audit sampling cadence.

Attached is our suggested DTIA attestation template (redwood_dtia-phased-attestation-template_v1.2.docx) and an evidence-index CSV with fields we typically ask for. Can you confirm:
- whether your legal team is comfortable with a short-form attestation (Phase B) for the limited categories, or whether you need a full UK IDTA/UK addendum path?
- expected internal sign-off timelines for procurement and security?

If helpful, Kimberly can propose language that maps directly to Novamed's existing DPA clauses to avoid redlines. Proposed owners at Redwood: Kimberly (contract language), Markus (technical routing), me (program lead).

Next step: can you share a preferred PO/DocuSign contact and whether Novamed will accept staged evidence (we can accept progressive uploads to the Drive link).

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Privacy Program Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +44 20 7946 0XXX
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novamed.es>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@novamed.es>, compliance@novamed.es
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Operationalizing tiered transfer controls — phased DTIA attestation & timeline

Hi Hannah,

Appreciate the clear breakdown — this phased approach looks reasonable. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- For Phase B, we can accept a short-form DTIA attestation but only if the attestation references our clause 4.2 (sensitive clinical metadata) and specifies technical guardrails (onshore fallback + logging).
- Procurement needs a sample DocuSign package and the full list of attachments that will be delivered to legal for review.
- Compliance asked whether Redwood will provide sampling evidence for the first 60 days after launch (we'd like a weekly snapshot).

I'll loop in our lead counsel (Contracts) formally if we move to redlines — leaving them on cc for visibility. Our target for internal signoff is 3 weeks but we may be able to compress to 10 business days if the DTIA wording is narrow.

Best,
Marta

--
Marta Ruiz
Head of Data Governance | Novamed
marta.ruiz@novamed.es
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novamed.es>, Contracts <contracts@novamed.es>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 14:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Operationalizing tiered transfer controls — phased DTIA attestation & timeline

Hi Marta — quick response and attaching proposed clause language that maps the short-form attestation to Novamed's clause 4.2.

Key points included in the draft:
- Narrow scope: only processing categories listed in Addendum A will use cross-border endpoints; all clinical identifiers will default to EU-only onshore routing.
- Fallback behavior: automatic onshore failover if KV-cache indicates routing outside EU for >30s (technical threshold we can tune).
- Evidence & sampling: Redwood will provide weekly sampling logs for 60 days post-launch and a month-by-month summary thereafter for any audit requests.

Attachment: redwood_dtia-phased-attestation-template_v1.2.docx (updated with clause map). Also included evidence-index-novamed.csv (fields: artifact_type, owner, timestamp, retention_location).

If Novamed is happy with the narrow scope, we can convert the doc to a DocuSign envelope (Laura — can you confirm who owns the DocuSign at Novamed? I'll prepare the packet).

Thanks,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novamed.es>, Contracts <contracts@novamed.es>

Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Operationalizing tiered transfer controls — phased DTIA attestation & timeline

Hi Marta / Contracts team — following up with next steps and owners.

Summary of agreed path (please confirm):
- Novamed confirms Addendum A processing categories by EOD Mon (05 Oct).
- Redwood provides updated DTIA (short-form) mapped to clause 4.2 and uploads to shared Drive by Tue (06 Oct).
- Contracts review window: 10 business days (aiming for DocuSign envelope by 19 Oct).
- Technical rollout: Markus will run a routing dry-run on 20 Oct and provide the first-week sampling snapshot on 27 Oct.

Deliverables included in the Drive folder: redwood_dtia-phased-attestation-template_v1.2.docx, evidence-index-novamed.csv, and a short technical runbook (routing-fallback-runbook.pdf) — I'll add them once Kimberly confirms final language.

If Novamed can confirm the Addendum A list and the procurement contact for DocuSign, we can hit the compressed 10-business-day target. Otherwise we will default to the three-week window Marta referenced.

Thanks all — happy to jump on a quick call to iron out any blocker.
